name: Digit 5
summary: Digit 5 is Agility Robotics' fifth-generation bipedal humanoid, unveiled on 15 September 2026 for manufacturing, warehouse and logistics work. Agility expects early customer access in the first half of 2027 and general availability by the end of 2027, including planned entry to the EU and UK.
specs_note: PROMOTED FROM IDENTITY DRAFT 2026-11-03 (HO-DATA Fast Lane intake). PUBLICATION OWNER-APPROVED 2026-11-03 (Robert Konecny, in thread). A new generation, kept separate from the existing 'Digit' record (agility-digit), whose deployments and specifications remain attributed to Digit 4. Values from Agility's launch release of 2026-09-15 (https://www.agilityrobotics.com/content/agility-unveils-digit-5-humanoid-robot-built-for-cooperatively-safe-work-at-scale): 'Digit 5 weighs 284 lb. (129 kg), stands 5' 11" (1.81 m)', 'repeatedly lift up to 50 lb. (22.7 kg) loads', 'A new 90-minute runtime battery system charges in just 9 minutes'. has_manipulation true: the release states it lifts loads and that a 'swappable gripper design ... allows Digit's tools to be changed'. Other capability booleans stay null (not stated in words). All figures are manufacturer-reported, pre-production values, not independently validated. RETRIEVAL: AGENT_ASSISTED_RESEARCH (docs/26) — retrieved 2026-11-03 by Claude Opus 5.5 (curl; processed page text) in a session initiated by Robert Konecny (HO-DATA Fast Lane intake, Digit 5). commercial_status_evidence.source_title: Agility Unveils Digit 5 Humanoid Robot Built for Cooperatively Safe Work at Scale
commercial_status_evidence.excerpt: In addition to the United States and Canada, for the first time, Agility plans to make Digit available for commercial deployment outside North America, starting with the European Union and United Kingdom. Digit 5 is expected to carry a CE mark and additional regulatory marks to enable market access to the EU, Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Early access to Digit 5 is expected to begin in the first half of 2027, with general availability for manufacturing, warehouse and distribution operators expected by the end of 2027.
commercial_status_evidence.note: ANNOUNCED = publicly revealed, no hardware shipping: early access and general availability are stated as future (H1 2027 / end-2027). EU and UK entry is a stated plan, not an offer: no availability_offers row is recorded for any region (no NOT_AVAILABLE either). CE marking is 'expected', not confirmed. The '$300 million in multi-year customer orders' is stated 'subject to satisfaction of certain contractual milestones'; it is not recorded as revenue or as a deployment. No Digit 5 customer deployment is recorded. RETRIEVAL: AGENT_ASSISTED_RESEARCH (docs/26) — retrieved 2026-11-03 by Claude Opus 5.5 (curl; processed page text) in a session initiated by Robert Konecny (HO-DATA Fast Lane intake, Digit 5). use_case_fits.notes: Agility's launch release (2026-09-15) names manufacturing among Digit 5's target markets and says Digit 5 will 'add more manipulation skills' to cover 'machine tending, kitting and sequencing, and quality inspection'. (https://www.agilityrobotics.com/content/agility-unveils-digit-5-humanoid-robot-built-for-cooperatively-safe-work-at-scale). HO-UC-01 evaluation (use_case_assessments/agility-digit-5.json).
use_case_fits.limitations: Announced, pre-production: no Digit 5 deployment, availability offer or price is recorded. Workflows beyond tote handling are planned by Agility, not demonstrated with Digit 5. Digit 4's commercial deployments (agility-digit) are not carried over. Safety certification is still in progress.

use_case_fits.notes: Agility's launch release (2026-09-15) names warehousing and logistics among Digit 5's target markets and describes workflows 'from depalletizing goods as they arrive ... and finally palletizing them for shipment', with tote handling. extended_specs.value: 90-minute runtime battery system charges in 9 minutes; 10:1 run-to-charge ratio; more than 20 hours of productive work in a 24-hour day
Height 1.81 m (5' 11"); can reach heights of up to 2.2 m (7.2 ft)
Swappable gripper design with ISO-standard mounting flanges
NVIDIA IGX Thor (stated as the exclusive onboard compute for the general availability version)

spec_caveats.text: Agility's launch release states 'repeatedly lift up to 50 lb. (22.7 kg) loads'; the product page rounds this to 'Payload* 23kg/50lbs' (footnote text not on the page). 22.7 kg recorded.
Left UNKNOWN: Agility states Digit 5 'can reach heights of up to 7.2 feet (2.2 m)', a maximum vertical reach, not the schema's single-arm reach. Recorded under body dimensions instead.
Agility states 'A new 90-minute runtime battery system charges in just 9 minutes'. Pre-production manufacturer figure.
